translations.text: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the churches of the Thessalonians, in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace and peace to you.
We give thanks to God for all of you, and we remember you in our prayers.
We remember without ceasing your works of faith, your labour of love, and your patient endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before God our Father.
Know, brothers beloved of God, that you have been chosen.
For our gospel did not come to you in vain, not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with great boldness of heart. You know what kind of people we were among you for your sake.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, for you received the word in much affliction, with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
so that you too became an example to all the believers who are in Macedonia and Achaia.
For the word of the Lord has spread out from you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia; your faith in God has also spread to every place, so that we no longer need to say anything.
They themselves tell about us, about the welcome we had among you, and how you turned from idols to serve the living and true God,
and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead: Jesus, who rescues us from the coming wrath.
You yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.
We had already suffered and been insulted at Philippi, as you know. Yet through our God we spoke boldly and openly to you the gospel of God, in the midst of great struggle.
For our appeal does not come from deceit or from impurity, nor is it made with trickery.
God has tested us and found us fit to be entrusted with the gospel, and so we speak. We do not speak to please people, but to please God, who tests our hearts.
For we never used words of flattery, as you know, nor a pretext for greed. God is our witness.
Nor did we seek glory from people, whether from you or from others. As apostles of Christ we could have done this and made ourselves a burden to you.
Instead we were humble among you, like a nurse caring for her own children.
We longed for you so much that we were glad to give you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls, for you had become dear to us.
Remember, brothers, our labour and toil. We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you, and in this way we preached the gospel of God to you.
You are witnesses, and so is God, of how worthily and blamelessly we behaved toward you believers.
As you know, we encouraged each one of you as a father encourages his child,
and we urged you to live in a way worthy of God, who has called you into his own kingdom and glory.

And for this reason I also thank God unceasingly: when you received from us the word of God that you heard, you accepted it not as the word of a human being but as what it truly is, the word of God. This word also shows its help among you who believe.
For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus. You suffered the same things from your own people as they did from the Jews,
who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out. They do not please God, and they are opposed to all people,
hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they might be saved. In this way they always fill up the measure of their sins. But wrath has come upon them completely.
But we, brothers, although we were orphaned from you for a short time, in face but not in heart, made all the more effort to see your face, with great longing.
For we wanted to come to you, I, Paul, once and twice, but the adversary hindered us.
For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? Is it not you, before the Lord Christ Jesus at his coming?
For you are our glory and joy.
Therefore, when we could no longer bear it, we thought it good to be left behind alone in Athens,
and we sent Timothy, our brother and God's servant in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and encourage you in your faith,
so that none of you would be troubled by these afflictions. For you know that this is what we are appointed for.
While we were still with you, we told you in advance that we were going to suffer affliction, and so it happened, as you know.
For this reason, when I could no longer bear it, I sent Timothy to find out about your faith, in case the tempter had somehow tempted you and our labor had been in vain.
But now Timothy has come to us from you and brought us good news of your faith and love. He reports that you always remember us kindly and long to see us, just as we long to see you.
Therefore, brothers, in all these sorrows and afflictions of yours we have been comforted about you through your faith,
for now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
How much thanks can we give to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God?
Night and day we pray all the more earnestly to see your face and to strengthen what is lacking in your faith.
Now may God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus direct our way to you.
And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all, just as we do toward you,
so that your hearts may be strengthened, blameless and in holiness, before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.
And now, brothers, I tell you and urge you in the Lord Jesus Christ: you learned from us how you ought to walk and to please God, so do so more and more.
For you know how many commandments we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
For this is the will of God: your sanctification, that you keep yourselves away from fornication,
that each one of you should know how to acquire his own vessel in holiness and honour,
not in the passion of lust, like the Gentiles who do not know God,
so that you do not transgress against your brother and defraud him in this matter. For the Lord is the avenger in all these things, as we told you beforehand and solemnly warned you.
For the Lord did not call us to uncleanness, but to holiness.
Therefore whoever disregards this disregards not a human being but God, who also gave his Holy Spirit upon you.
But concerning brotherly love we have no need to write to you, for all of you are taught by God to love one another,
and indeed you do this toward all the brothers who are throughout Macedonia. I urge you, brothers, to do so still more,
and to be eager for honour: be quiet, mind your own affairs, and work with your own hands, as we commanded you,
so that you may conduct yourselves properly toward those outside and may need nothing from anyone.
I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you do not grieve like the others, who have no hope.
If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
We tell you this by the word of the Lord: that we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep,
for the Lord himself will come down from heaven with a command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first;
and only then will we who are alive, who are left, be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we will be with the Lord forever.
Therefore comfort one another with these words.
But concerning the times and the years, brothers, we have no need to write to you,
for you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
When they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them, like labour pains on a woman giving birth, and they will not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, for that day to overtake you like a thief.
For you are all children of light and children of the day; we are not of the night or of darkness.
So let us not sleep as others do, but let us stay alert and keep watch.
For those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But since we belong to the day, let us stay alert and put on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of hope and of salvation.
For God did not make us for wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with him.
Therefore comfort one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.
I beg you, brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you, who are your leaders in the Lord and your teachers,
and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. And be at peace with them.
I beg you, brothers, instruct the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward everyone.
Take care that none of you repays anyone evil for evil; rather, always pursue what is good toward one another and toward everyone.
Rejoice always.
Pray without ceasing.
Give thanks in everything, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
Do not trouble the Spirit.
Do not despise prophecy.
Test everything, and hold fast to what is better.
Keep away from every evil deed.
And may the God of peace himself make you holy in all perfection and all life, and may he keep your spirit, heart, and body blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Faithful is he who called you, and he will also do it.
Brothers, pray for us as well.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I adjure you by the Lord: read this letter to all the brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
